To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) shear thinning carrier suspensions are effective to enhance mobility of MZVI, and that (2) the transport of iron colloids can be predicted by a coupled hydrological-transport model, provided that deposition and mechanical filtration phenomena are accounted for.

(i) the transport of highly viscous slurries of iron particles is strongly affected by the rheological properties of the carrier fluid; (ii) the transport is also strongly affected by deposition phenomena and mechanical filtration; (iii) these phenomena depend on the size of the particles, thus affecting the transport of micro and nanoscale iron particles in a different way.
• the transport of highly viscous slurries of iron based particles (MZVI and NZVI) in porous media is affected by the deposition of particles onto the soil matrix, and by mechanical filtration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an integrated experimental and modeling approach to the study of the transport and fate of colloidal suspensions of iron nanoparticles for in situ groundwater remediations.
the development of a comprehensive model for the transport of shear thinning colloidal slurries in porous media.

the development of a transport model for iron based colloids, that is able to predict the radius of influence of the injection points and the long term stability of the injected materials, in the context of groundwater remediation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of highly concentrated slurried iron colloids for in situ groundwater remediations is a promising technology, provided that: 1) The colloidal suspension is properly prepared and injected, 2) The injection is performed under the right hydrogeological and hydrogeochemical conditions (i.e. avoiding clogging and mechanical filtration), and 3) The colloidal stability is monitored during the treatment, in order to avoid the formation of large aggregates, which can cause clogging and/or filtration.

, for the specific experimental conditions, the model is capable of predicting the breakthrough curve for the colloids and the clogging effect of the injected particles, thus providing a reliable estimation of radius of influence of the injection points and the time required for the complete remediation.

the transport of iron colloids in porous media is a complex process that is strongly dependent upon particle size, concentration and rheological properties of the carrier fluid, as well as hydrodynamic properties of the porous medium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of highly concentrated slururies of MZVI or NZVI in shear thinning carrier liquids is not recommended for groundwater remediation, as it may result in clogging of the soil.

the use of highly concentrated suspensions of MZVI or NZVI, injected in shear thinning carrier solutions, can be effective for remediation of highly contaminated aquifers, but only if a correct dimensioning is carried out.

the use of highly concentrated slurried iron based colloids can be a valid option for groundwater remediation, but the transport model developed in this work is required to predict the mobility of the injected particles and to avoid clogging of the porous medium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of non Newtonian carrier fluids is not a panacea for the mobility problems of colloidal suspensions of MZVI/NZVI.

, for a reliable prediction of the radius of transport of colloidal particles injected in the ground, the model has to be able to account for the complex interplay between the colloidal transport, deposition and mechanical filtration.

the transport of iron based colloidal suspensions is a very complex process, and that the use of shear thinning carrier liquids is not sufficient to guarantee the long term mobility of these materials, if not coupled with a careful selection of the hydrochemical conditions.
